RQ1: RQ1: Does the combination of Ichimoku and vision agentic portfolio improve overall cumulative net return and annualized daily-return Sharpe relative to Bitcoin buy-and-hold, equal-weight cryptocurrency, large-cap equal weight, and top-three momentum over the common walk-forward validation period? In addition, does combining Ichimoku technical signals and chart-based vision improve cumulative net return and annualized daily-return Sharpe relative to Ichimoku-only and vision-only configurations?
H1: H1: The combined technical and vision configuration is expected to beat both the technical-only and vision-only configurations on cumulative net return and on annualized Sharpe ratio from daily returns. In a supplementary comparison with regime and sector adjustments turned off in all three arms, the claim is treated as statistically confirmed only if, against both single-signal arms, the paired confidence interval for the Sharpe difference is above zero and the Holm-adjusted p-value is below .05.
RQ2: RQ2: Does the regime-and-sector portfolio improve net risk-adjusted performance and downside behavior relative to the unmodified technical–vision baseline, and what do the configured regime and LLM-layer studies reveal about that effect?
H2: H2: Holding the signal inputs, rebalancing schedule and execution assumptions the same, adding regime and sector adjustments is expected to raise cumulative net return and annualized Sharpe and lower maximum drawdown compared with the base process.
RQ3: RQ3: Does the constrained SAC implementation improve risk-adjusted performance and maximum drawdown outcomes relative to the weekly agentic baseline across all sixteen validation windows?
H3: H3: Relative to the weekly agentic baseline, the complete SAC implementation will have a higher annualized daily-return Sharpe, a smaller full-period maximum drawdown, and lower local maximum drawdown in a majority of the sixteen windows. Cumulative net return, volatility, turnover, costs, and paired uncertainty intervals provide supporting evidence. Because SAC refreshes targets every fifteen minutes, this expectation concerns the complete implementation rather than the isolated effect of learned exposure scaling.
RQ4: RQ4: How does the original SAC overlay’s mean exposure vary across the five reported drawdown bands (below 5%, 5%–below 10%, 10%–below 15%, 15%–below 20%, and at least 20%), and what exposure differences and limit violations occur across its sixteen validation windows?
H4: H4: Mean cryptocurrency exposure is expected to be lower during severe drawdowns (at least 20%) than during minimal drawdowns (below 5%) across the original sixteen windows. The severe-versus-minimal exposure contrast is interpreted descriptively. Compliance with the programmed exposure limits tests implementation behavior, not whether SAC learned effective risk management. The original summaries pair exposure with post-return fold drawdown; they do not by themselves identify a response to pre-action risk.
